newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ACTU wage claim inflationary, would cause job losses - govt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ACTU wage claim inflationary, would cause job losses - govt.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Monday there would be a rise in inflation and a loss of jobs if the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) won its minimum wage claim.

"The implications of the ACTU's claim, if granted, would be a big jump in the rate of inflation and would jeopardise a lot of jobs," Reith told parliament. The ACTU's living wage claim to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission calls for an 8.75 percent rise in minimum weekly earnings.

The Treasury had done preliminary work on the ACTU's claim, allowing for a monetary tightening to keep the underlying inflation rate within its target range of two to three percent, Reith said. The impact of the first stage of the claim would mean the unemployment rate would increase by 0.25 of a percentage point in 1997/98, rising by a further 0.5 of a percentage point for each year to 1999/00, he said.
"It would cause a cumulative loss of GDP growth of 2.25 percentage points over these three financial years," he said.
The preliminary advice also found there would be an even bigger impact with all three stages of the ACTU's claim.

The unemployment rate would rise 0.25 of a percentage point in 1997/98, one percentage point in 1998/99 and 1.75 percentage points in 1999/00. "It would mean overall to the economy a cumulative loss of GDP growth of five percentage points from 1997/98 to 1999/00," Reith said.
The government is offering an A$8 a week wage rise for low paid workers on awards less than averge weekly ordinary time earnings, compared with the ACTU's offer of A$20 a week for low paid workers.
The conservative Liberal-National government said it would give further details before making its submission to the commission hearing on the wage claim scheduled for November 27.
Under existing minimum wage rates, some low-paid workers in the metal industry earn about A$350 per week.
